decisions.reason: The question names correspondence hallucination and asks whether it improves absolute pose estimation. It leaves the partial-overlap setting and the occluded and out-of-view keypoints implicit. Those details appear in the method.

The method gives the inputs, the target-plane probability distribution per source keypoint, and the three visibility cases. It omits the shared CNN, learned target-descriptor padding, cross-attention, and positional encoding. It also leaves the identification, inpainting, and outpainting terms unexplained.
The poster omits Neural Reprojection Error, the negative log-likelihood at the reprojected location, the training depth and pose inputs, and the fact that visibility-class labels are unnecessary.

ScanNet is named for the pose result. The poster omits the indoor and outdoor training dataset roles, the distinction between held-out quantitative tests and qualitative transfer examples, and the correspondence protocol of 2,500 pairs per dataset with 2% to 80% overlap.

The poster omits both correspondence results on held-out ScanNet and MegaDepth scenes: lower NRE than the uniform map and argmax pixel errors below the mean random-prediction error for all three tasks.

LoFTR, DRCNet, and S2D appear in the pose figure legend. The poster omits their inpainting and outpainting comparison on ScanNet and MegaDepth, the pixel-distance score, and the target-image search boundary.

The figure includes identity and feature-matching baselines for ScanNet pairs with 2% to 5% overlap. It varies the rotation and translation thresholds. The required 2,500 held-out pairs, source depth and correspondence-map inputs, cumulative 2%-to-x% overlap score, and both fixed threshold pairs are missing.

The poster shows the low-overlap advantage. It omits the overall robustness result, the comparison showing the largest advantage at low overlap, the ablation finding that outpainting drove the gain and inpainting added little, and the slight advantage for local matching at high overlap.

The limitations strip contains an incomplete sentence about quadratic attention complexity. It omits the precision limit from low-resolution maps, the finite padding reach, the less-peaked inpainting maps, and the caveat about noisy MegaDepth inpainting labels.

notes: The 2%–5% range describes the displayed pose experiment and agrees with its caption. The required correspondence overlap range and fixed pose thresholds are missing conditions. The pose figure supports the narrow result it accompanies. Its axis labels and legend are small at the supplied image size, while the section headings and main text are easy to locate. The limitations sentence ends at “see Sec.” in both the image and editable text, so it was counted as incomplete copy. No layout overflow is visible. These judgments are based on the supplied export and text.
